Problem Domain:
Industrial IoT (IIoT), Predictive Maintenance (PdM), Sensor Data Analysis, Time Series Analysis, Anomaly Detection, Deep Learning.

Project Description:
This project develops a system for monitoring the health of industrial equipment based on multivariate sensor data and predicting potential failures for proactive maintenance scheduling. It utilizes Pandas for handling and processing high-frequency time series data from multiple sensors attached to a piece of equipment. Statsmodels is employed for classical time series analysis, feature engineering (e.g., decomposition, autocorrelation features), and potentially as a baseline forecasting/anomaly detection method. The core predictive component uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, implemented in PyTorch or TensorFlow/Keras, to model the complex temporal dependencies in the sensor readings and predict either the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the equipment or the probability of failure within a future time window. The system aims to detect subtle anomalies preceding failures and provide actionable insights for maintenance planning, reducing downtime and costs.

Frameworks Used:

  • Core Data: Pandas, NumPy
  • Time Series Analysis: Statsmodels (e.g., tsa.seasonal_decompose, tsa.stattools)
  • Deep Learning: PyTorch or TensorFlow/Keras (for LSTM model definition, training, inference)
  • Machine Learning (Helpers): Scikit-learn (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, metrics like RMSE/MAE for RUL, classification metrics for failure prediction)
  • Data Acquisition: Pandas (read_csv, read_sql), potentially libraries for specific industrial protocols (e.g., MQTT, OPC-UA) or databases (e.g., InfluxDB, TimescaleDB).
  • Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly (for sensor data, predictions, RUL curves)
  • Configuration: YAML

Dataset:
Access to real industrial sensor data leading up to failures is often proprietary. We will use a well-known public dataset for predictive maintenance, such as the NASA Turbofan Engine Degradation Simulation Data Set.

  • Source: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence Data Repository: Turbofan Engine Degradation Simulation Data Set
  • Characteristics: Multivariate time series data from simulated turbofan engines under different operating conditions and fault modes. Includes sensor readings (temperature, pressure, speed, etc.) and the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for each engine cycle in the training set.
import pandas as pd

import logging

# Configure logging

# --- NASA Turbofan Dataset Download (Example for FD001) ---
# URLs might change, check the NASA repository page if links break.
NASA_DATA_URL_BASE = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mahshadkh/keras-predictive-maintenance/master/data/CMAPSSData/"
DATASET_FILES = {
    "train": "train_FD001.txt",

LOCAL_DATA_DIR = "./data/cmapss_fd001"

def download_and_extract_cmapss(base_url: str, files: Dict[str, str], local_dir: str) -> bool:
    """Downloads and saves CMAPSS dataset files."""
    os.makedirs(local_dir, exist_ok=True)
    all_successful = True
    for key, filename in files.items():
        file_url = base_url + filename
        local_path = os.path.join(local_dir, filename)
        if os.path.exists(local_path):
            logging.info(f"File {filename} already exists locally.")
            continue
        logging.info(f"Downloading {filename} from {file_url}...")
        try:
            response = requests.get(file_url)
            response.raise_for_status()
            with open(local_path,     w   ) as f:
                f.write(response.text)
            logging.info(f"Saved {filename} to {local_path}")
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to download {filename}: {e}")
            all_successful = False
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error saving {filename}: {e}")
            all_successful = False
    return all_successful

def load_cmapss_data(local_dir: str, files: Dict[str, str]) -> Optional[Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]]:
    """Loads the downloaded CMAPSS data into Pandas DataFrames."""
    data = {}
    # Define column names based on dataset description
    op_settings = ["op_setting_1", "op_setting_2", "op_setting_3"]
    sensors = [f"sensor_{i}" for i in range(1, 22)] # 21 sensors
    cols_train_test = ["unit_number", "time_cycles"] + op_settings + sensors
    cols_rul = ["RUL"]

    try:
        for key, filename in files.items():
            local_path = os.path.join(local_dir, filename)
            if not os.path.exists(local_path):
                 logging.error(f"File not found: {local_path}. Cannot load data.")
                 return None
            logging.info(f"Loading {filename}...")
            if key == "rul":
                df = pd.read_csv(local_path, sep="\s+", header=None, names=cols_rul)
            else:
                df = pd.read_csv(local_path, sep="\s+", header=None, names=cols_train_test)
            data[key] = df
            logging.info(f"Loaded {key} data. Shape: {df.shape}")
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        logging.error(f"Error loading data from {local_dir}: {e}")
        return None

# Download and load data
if download_and_extract_cmapss(NASA_DATA_URL_BASE, DATASET_FILES, LOCAL_DATA_DIR):
    cmapss_data: Optional[Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]] = load_cmapss_data(LOCAL_DATA_DIR, DATASET_FILES)
else:
    logging.error("Failed to download all required dataset files.")
    cmapss_data = None

if cmapss_data is not None:
    print("Sample CMAPSS Training Data (FD001):")
    print(cmapss_data[    train   ].head())
    print("\nSample CMAPSS Test Data (FD001):")
    print(cmapss_data[    test    ].head())
    print("\nSample CMAPSS RUL Data (FD001) - RUL for test units:")
    print(cmapss_data[    rul ].head())
    # --- Add RUL to training data --- 
    # Calculate RUL for training units (time_to_failure)
    max_cycles = cmapss_data[    train   ].groupby(  unit_number )[  time_cycles ].max()
    cmapss_data[    train   ] = cmapss_data[    train   ].merge(max_cycles.rename(  max_cycle   ), 
                                                      left_on=    unit_number , right_index=True)
    cmapss_data[    train   ][  RUL ] = cmapss_data[    train   ][  max_cycle   ] - cmapss_data[    train   ][  time_cycles ]
    cmapss_data[    train   ].drop(columns=[    max_cycle   ], inplace=True)
    print("\nTraining Data with calculated RUL:")
    print(cmapss_data[    train   ].head())
else:
    print("Failed to load CMAPSS dataset.")

Use Cases:

  1. Remaining Useful Life (RUL) Prediction: Estimate the number of operational cycles or time remaining before a piece of equipment is likely to fail.
  2. Failure Prediction: Predict the probability of failure within a specific future window (e.g., next 100 cycles, next week).
  3. Anomaly Detection: Identify sensor readings or patterns that deviate significantly from normal operating behavior, potentially indicating incipient faults.
  4. Condition Monitoring Dashboard: Visualize sensor trends, health indices, detected anomalies, and RUL predictions for operators and maintenance teams.
  5. Optimized Maintenance Scheduling: Use RUL predictions to schedule maintenance just before failure, minimizing downtime and avoiding unnecessary early interventions.
  6. Root Cause Analysis Support: Analyze sensor patterns associated with anomalies or predicted failures to help diagnose the underlying fault.

  7. Validation & Testing (6-9 weeks): Validate model performance on hold-out data using appropriate metrics (RMSE/MAE for RUL, Precision/Recall/F1/AUC for failure prediction). Test the system under simulated operational conditions. Validate anomaly detection performance.
  8. Deployment & Monitoring (5-7 weeks): Deploy the system (e.g., edge device, cloud platform). Set up monitoring for data quality, model performance (concept drift), prediction latency, and system health. Develop dashboards for visualization.
  9. Operational Use & Refinement (Ongoing): Utilize the system for maintenance planning and operational monitoring. Collect feedback from maintenance teams. Retrain models periodically with new data and failure information. Continuously refine features and models.

# --- Filename: industrial_sensor_health_monitoring_pred_maint.py ---

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import logging
import os
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional, Any

# ML/DL
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset
import joblib # For saving scaler

# Visualization
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Configuration
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(module)s - %(message)s")

# --- Constants & Config ---
# Data Config (assuming CMAPSS FD001 data loaded into `cmapss_data` dict)
DATA_DIR = "./data/cmapss_fd001"
UNIT_COL = "unit_number"
TIME_COL = "time_cycles"
TARGET_COL = "RUL"
OP_SETTINGS = ["op_setting_1", "op_setting_2", "op_setting_3"]
SENSORS = [f"sensor_{i}" for i in range(1, 22)]
FEATURES_TO_USE = OP_SETTINGS + SENSORS # Select features

# LSTM Config
SEQUENCE_LENGTH = 50 # Lookback window size
HIDDEN_SIZE = 100
NUM_LAYERS = 2
BATCH_SIZE = 64
NUM_EPOCHS = 30 # Reduce for faster example
LEARNING_RATE = 0.001
DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Paths
SCALER_PATH = "./models/pdm_scaler.joblib"
MODEL_PATH = "./models/pdm_lstm_model.pt"

# --- Data Preparation --- 
def prepare_data_for_lstm(df: pd.DataFrame, features: List[str], target: str, 
                          sequence_length: int, scaler: Optional[MinMaxScaler] = None) 
                          -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, MinMaxScaler]:
    """Scales data and creates sequences for LSTM."""
    logging.info(f"Preparing data for LSTM with sequence length {sequence_length}...")

    # Scale features
    if scaler is None:
        scaler = MinMaxScaler()
        scaled_features = scaler.fit_transform(df[features])
    else:
        scaled_features = scaler.transform(df[features])

    scaled_data = pd.DataFrame(scaled_features, columns=features, index=df.index)
    scaled_data[UNIT_COL] = df[UNIT_COL]
    scaled_data[target] = df[target]

    sequences = []
    labels = []
    # Group by unit to create sequences within each unit's lifecycle
    for unit_id in scaled_data[UNIT_COL].unique():
        unit_data = scaled_data[scaled_data[UNIT_COL] == unit_id]
        unit_features = unit_data[features].values
        unit_target = unit_data[target].values

        # Create sequences
        for i in range(len(unit_data) - sequence_length):
            sequences.append(unit_features[i:i+sequence_length])
            labels.append(unit_target[i+sequence_length-1]) # RUL at the end of the sequence

    X = np.array(sequences)
    y = np.array(labels)
    logging.info(f"Created sequences. X shape: {X.shape}, y shape: {y.shape}")
    return X, y, scaler

# --- PyTorch LSTM Model & Dataset ---
class SensorDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, sequences, labels):
        self.sequences = torch.tensor(sequences, dtype=torch.float32)
        self.labels = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1) # Add dim for regression target

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.sequences)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        return self.sequences[idx], self.labels[idx]

class RUL_LSTM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_size, num_layers, output_size=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.num_layers = num_layers
        # Use batch_first=True for (batch, seq, feature) input shape
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(input_size, hidden_size, num_layers, batch_first=True, dropout=0.2 if num_layers > 1 else 0)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_size, output_size)
        # Optional: Add activation like ReLU if RUL is always positive
        # self.relu = nn.ReLU()

    def forward(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch_size, seq_length, input_size)
        h0 = torch.zeros(self.num_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_size).to(x.device)
        c0 = torch.zeros(self.num_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_size).to(x.device)

        out, _ = self.lstm(x, (h0, c0))

        # Get output from the last time step of the sequence
        out = out[:, -1, :]
        out = self.fc(out)
        # out = self.relu(out) # Optional
        return out

# --- Training Function ---
def train_lstm_model(model, dataloader, criterion, optimizer, num_epochs, device):
    logging.info(f"Starting LSTM training for {num_epochs} epochs on {device}...")
    model.train() # Set model to training mode
    train_losses = []
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        epoch_loss = 0.0
        for i, (sequences, labels) in enumerate(dataloader):
            sequences = sequences.to(device)
            labels = labels.to(device)

            # Forward pass
            outputs = model(sequences)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

            # Backward and optimize
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            epoch_loss += loss.item()

        avg_epoch_loss = epoch_loss / len(dataloader)
        train_losses.append(avg_epoch_loss)
        if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0 or epoch == 0:
             logging.info(f    Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], Loss: {avg_epoch_loss:.4f}  )
    logging.info("Training finished.")
    return train_losses

# --- Evaluation Function ---
def evaluate_lstm_model(model, dataloader, criterion, device):
    logging.info(f"Evaluating LSTM model on {device}...")
    model.eval() # Set model to evaluation mode
    all_preds = []
    all_labels = []
    total_loss = 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for sequences, labels in dataloader:
            sequences = sequences.to(device)
            labels = labels.to(device)
            outputs = model(sequences)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            all_preds.append(outputs.cpu().numpy())
            all_labels.append(labels.cpu().numpy())

    avg_loss = total_loss / len(dataloader)
    all_preds = np.concatenate(all_preds).flatten()
    all_labels = np.concatenate(all_labels).flatten()

    rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(all_labels, all_preds))
    mae = mean_absolute_error(all_labels, all_preds)
    logging.info(f"Evaluation Results - Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}, RMSE: {rmse:.4f}, MAE: {mae:.4f}")
    return avg_loss, rmse, mae, all_labels, all_preds

# --- Main Execution Logic ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.info("--- Starting Industrial Sensor PdM Pipeline --- ")

    if cmapss_data is None:
        logging.error("CMAPSS data not loaded. Exiting.")
        exit()

    train_df = cmapss_data[    train   ]
    test_df = cmapss_data[    test    ]
    rul_df = cmapss_data[    rul ]

    # 1. Prepare Training Data
    X_train, y_train, scaler = prepare_data_for_lstm(train_df, FEATURES_TO_USE, TARGET_COL, SEQUENCE_LENGTH)
    # Save the scaler
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(SCALER_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(scaler, SCALER_PATH)
    logging.info(f"Scaler saved to {SCALER_PATH}")

    train_dataset = SensorDataset(X_train, y_train)
    train_dataloader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=True)

    # 2. Initialize Model, Loss, Optimizer
    input_size = X_train.shape[2] # Number of features
    model = RUL_LSTM(input_size, HIDDEN_SIZE, NUM_LAYERS).to(DEVICE)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss() # Mean Squared Error for RUL regression
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=LEARNING_RATE)
    logging.info(f"LSTM Model Initialized:\n{model}")

    # 3. Train the Model
    if not os.path.exists(MODEL_PATH):
        train_losses = train_lstm_model(model, train_dataloader, criterion, optimizer, NUM_EPOCHS, DEVICE)
        # Save the trained model
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), MODEL_PATH)
        logging.info(f"Trained LSTM model saved to {MODEL_PATH}")
        # Plot training loss
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
        plt.plot(train_losses)
        plt.title("Training Loss Curve")
        plt.xlabel("Epoch")
        plt.ylabel("MSE Loss")
        plt.show()
    else:
        logging.info(f"Loading pre-trained model from {MODEL_PATH}")
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(MODEL_PATH, map_location=DEVICE))

    # 4. Prepare Test Data
    # For test data, we need the RUL for the *last* sequence of each unit
    # Group test data by unit, take the last SEQUENCE_LENGTH readings for each
    test_sequences = []
    true_rul_for_test = []
    test_units = test_df[UNIT_COL].unique()

    # Scale test data using the *same* scaler fitted on training data
    scaled_test_features = scaler.transform(test_df[FEATURES_TO_USE])
    scaled_test_df = pd.DataFrame(scaled_test_features, columns=FEATURES_TO_USE, index=test_df.index)
    scaled_test_df[UNIT_COL] = test_df[UNIT_COL]

    for unit_id in test_units:
        unit_data = scaled_test_df[scaled_test_df[UNIT_COL] == unit_id]
        unit_features = unit_data[FEATURES_TO_USE].values
        if len(unit_features) >= SEQUENCE_LENGTH:
            test_sequences.append(unit_features[-SEQUENCE_LENGTH:])
            # RUL corresponds to the unit ID (index in rul_df is unit_id - 1)
            true_rul_for_test.append(rul_df.iloc[unit_id - 1][TARGET_COL])
        else:
            logging.warning(f"Unit {unit_id} in test set has less than {SEQUENCE_LENGTH} cycles. Skipping.")

    X_test = np.array(test_sequences)
    y_test_actual = np.array(true_rul_for_test)

    if len(X_test) == 0:
         logging.error("No valid test sequences generated. Cannot evaluate.")
    else:
         test_dataset = SensorDataset(X_test, y_test_actual) # Labels used only for evaluation convenience
         test_dataloader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False)

         # 5. Evaluate on Test Data
         test_loss, test_rmse, test_mae, test_labels, test_preds = evaluate_lstm_model(model, test_dataloader, criterion, DEVICE)
         logging.info(f"Final Test Set Performance - RMSE: {test_rmse:.4f}, MAE: {test_mae:.4f}")

         # 6. Visualize Predictions vs Actual RUL
         plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
         plt.scatter(test_labels, test_preds, alpha=0.5)
         plt.plot([min(test_labels), max(test_labels)], [min(test_labels), max(test_labels)],     r-- , color=    red , label="Ideal")
         plt.xlabel("Actual RUL")
         plt.ylabel("Predicted RUL")
         plt.title(f"Predicted vs Actual RUL on Test Set (RMSE: {test_rmse:.2f})")
         plt.legend()
         plt.grid(True)
         plt.show()

    logging.info("--- PdM Pipeline Finished --- ")

Where to Go From Here (Improvements):

  1. Advanced LSTM Architectures: Explore Bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTMs), LSTMs with Attention mechanisms, or Convolutional LSTMs (ConvLSTMs) to potentially capture more complex patterns.
  2. Feature Engineering with Statsmodels: Incorporate more features derived from statsmodels, such as trend/seasonality components from decomposition, autocorrelation features, or results from statistical tests for stationarity/changes.
  3. Hybrid Models: Combine LSTMs with other models, e.g., using CNNs to extract spatial features from sensor correlations before feeding into an LSTM, or combining LSTM predictions with physics-based degradation models.
  4. Uncertainty Quantification: Use techniques like Monte Carlo Dropout or Bayesian LSTMs to estimate the uncertainty associated with RUL predictions, providing confidence intervals.
  5. Multi-Task Learning: Train a single model to simultaneously predict RUL and classify failure modes, potentially improving performance on both tasks.
  6. Anomaly Detection Integration: Use the LSTM's reconstruction error (difference between input and output of an autoencoder variant) or prediction error as an anomaly score for early fault detection.
  7. Transfer Learning: Pre-train models on large datasets (like multiple subsets of CMAPSS or other similar datasets) and fine-tune them for specific equipment or operating conditions with limited data.
  8. Online Learning/Adaptation: Develop methods for updating the model incrementally as new data arrives, allowing it to adapt to changing equipment behavior or operating conditions without full retraining.
  9. Scalability for High-Frequency Data: Optimize data loading and sequence preparation for very high-frequency sensor data, potentially using libraries like tsfresh for automated feature extraction or Dask/Spark for distributed processing.
  10. Explainability (XAI): Apply techniques like SHAP or LIME adapted for time series/RNNs to understand which sensors or time steps contribute most to a particular RUL prediction or anomaly score.
